verify_xue2025_icccs_dcformer.official_abstract_verbatim: The integrated sensing and communication (ISAC) technology is considered as one of the key features of 6 G networks, with potential far surpassing that of traditional singlefunction systems. At present, there are serious difficulties in the identification of birds and small unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs) in urban low-altitude scenes. How to use existing base stations and ISAC technology to identify UAVs and birds becomes a new challenge. In order to classify the radar echo images of UAV and bird more accurately, we collected the echo data of rotor UAV and bird through simulation and actual measurement using 5G signals, and performed short-time Fourier transform (STFT) on the data to obtain the spectrograms of the micro-Doppler signatures. We propose a classification method, DC-Former network, which can accurately capture the channel information of the image and periodically extract effective features according to the object's micro-motion. By putting the spectrograms into the DC-Former network, we can extract the effective features and classification results of the target. The experimental results show that compared with the existing classification methods, the DCFormer network can obtain more accurate classification accuracy, so as to effectively distinguish the radar echo images of UAVs and birds.

claim_by_claim_verification.corroboration: Same BUPT group's companion paper - Wei, Ma, He, Zhang, Feng, Liu, Liang, 'UAV's Rotor Micro-Doppler Feature Extraction Using ISAC Signal: Algorithm Design and Testbed Evaluation', IEEE Trans. Wireless Commun., vol. 24, no. 12, pp. 10166-10182, Dec. 2025 (local copy: /data/public/sionna_jeong/papers_isac_sionna/paper_sionna_Ray_0723/UAVs_Rotor_Micro-Doppler_Feature_Extraction_Using_Integrated_Sensing_and_Communication_Signal_Algorithm_Design_and_Testbed_Evaluation.pdf). Its Sec. V states: 'The proposed algorithm is validated on the Sub-6G ISAC hardware testbed. The ISAC system is based on the 5G NR protocol and consists of UL and DL baseband signal processing, intermediate frequency modulation, 3.5 GHz RF modulation, and antenna modules.' Subcarrier spacing 30 kHz. Test location Ningbo, China. I did NOT find '100 MHz' anywhere in that paper's text.
claim_by_claim_verification.note: So the DC-Former measurements were almost certainly taken on this same 3.5 GHz Sub-6G 5G NR testbed, but that is inference from the sibling paper, not from the DC-Former text.

corrections.severity: MATERIAL - affects how we may cite this paper
corrections.what: The dataset is SIMULATION + MEASUREMENT MIXED, not purely real measured data.
corrections.the_wrong_version: Survey 2604.02680 SS III-C prose: 'To address the limitations of simulated datasets, they collect real radar echo data of rotor UAVs and birds using 5G NR signals' - this drops the simulation half and reads as a purely measured dataset. The task brief inherited this error ('시뮬 데이터셋의 한계를 인정하고 실제 레이다 에코를 직접 수집').
corrections.the_original: Abstract: 'we collected the echo data of rotor UAV and bird through simulation AND actual measurement using 5G signals'
corrections.note: The survey CONTRADICTS ITSELF: its own Table VIII row for Xue et al. [92] correctly says 'Simulation and measured radar echo data using 5G NR signals at 3.5 GHz, 100 MHz bandwidth'. So the survey's table is right and its prose is wrong.
corrections.consequence: We cannot cite this as 'a fully measured 5G NR drone-vs-bird micro-Doppler dataset'. The 10,000/class split between simulated and measured is UNKNOWN from the abstract, and may be mostly synthetic.

corrections.detail: The abstract says '5G signals'. '5G NR' is the survey's sharpening (defensible given the group's NR testbed, but not verbatim).
Survey says 10,000 per class for each of UAV and bird. The 20,000 total is downstream arithmetic. Neither the abstract nor the survey prints '20,000'.

S2 normalizes the venue to 'International Conference on Communication, Computing & Security' - WRONG. Crossref is authoritative: '2025 10th International Conference on Computer and Communication System (ICCCS)', Chengdu. Do not trust S2's venue string here.

relevance_to_our_questions.Q1_passive_sensing: NOT a passive-sensing paper. This is base-station ISAC ('How to use existing base stations and ISAC technology'), i.e. the transmitter is cooperative and the same system does sensing. Do NOT list under passive bistatic.
relevance_to_our_questions.Q2_microdoppler_with_OFDM: RELEVANT but weak evidence. It is 5G-signal micro-Doppler with STFT, with some real measurement, and drone-vs-bird is exactly the discrimination problem. However: 6-page minor conference, closed access, 2 citations, no reproducible numbers verifiable from outside the paywall.
relevance_to_our_questions.Q3_deep_learning_framework: RELEVANT as a design datapoint: depthwise-conv + Transformer hybrid on STFT spectrograms for binary drone/bird. But since we cannot open the body, we cannot copy its architecture or training recipe. Prefer the sibling papers we CAN read in full: AirGuard (arXiv:2603.13112, JSAC-accepted, CNN + cmD + HRRP dual fusion, 237600 samples, SIMULATION ONLY) and Wei et al. IEEE TWC 24(12):10166-10182 (real 3.5 GHz 5G NR Sub-6G testbed, rotor micro-Doppler extraction, Ningbo).

verify_xue2025_icccs_dcformer.recommended_citation_language_for_our_re: Xue et al. (ICCCS 2025, pp. 927-932, BUPT) report a depthwise-convolution + Transformer hybrid ('DC-Former') classifying drone-vs-bird from STFT micro-Doppler spectrograms built from 5G-signal echoes gathered by BOTH simulation and measurement. We were unable to obtain the full text (closed access, no preprint), so the frequently repeated '96-98% accuracy' and '10,000 spectrograms per class' figures are traceable only to the secondary survey arXiv:2604.02680, not to the original.
